text:
This figure comprises four demographic charts presenting a profile of a board or leadership group across four categories: **AGE**, **GENDER**, **RACE**, and **TENURE**. 

* **AGE** is displayed using a donut chart categorizing individuals into age groups by decade (30s through 70s) alongside the average age.
* **GENDER** is shown as a horizontal bar chart comparing female and male representation.
* **RACE** is depicted as a vertical bar chart distinguishing between White and racially diverse members, with an accompanying text legend specifying Asian American, African American, and Hispanic representation.
* **TENURE** is illustrated through a pie chart divided into service length brackets (0–5 years, 5–10 years, and >10 years), accompanied by the average tenure in years.

This is a line chart titled "Total Return Performance" comparing the stock performance of Columbia Banking System, Inc. against the KBW Nasdaq Regional Banking Index. The horizontal axis covers an annual timeframe from December 31, 2017, to December 31, 2022, with the vertical axis representing the Index Value starting from a base of 100. Both series track closely together from late 2017 through 2020; after 2020, the KBW Nasdaq Regional Banking Index rises significantly to peak at the end of 2021 before declining slightly in 2022, while Columbia Banking System, Inc. trends downward through 2022.

This dual-axis combination bar and line chart compares executive compensation against total shareholder return across fiscal years 2020, 2021, and 2022. The left vertical axis measures "Compensation Actually Paid ($M)" using bar graphs for "CEO CAP" and "Average Non-CEO NEO CAP," while the right vertical axis tracks "Total Shareholder Return" using line graphs for "COLB TSR" and a peer benchmark ("KRX TSR"). Overall, executive compensation generally increases from 2020 to 2022, while the company's total shareholder return (COLB TSR) shows a slight gradual decline over the same three-year period.

This dual-axis chart combines a grouped bar graph and a line graph to illustrate executive compensation alongside net income over three fiscal years (FY2020 through FY2022). The left vertical axis tracks "Compensation Actually Paid ($M)" using light blue bars for CEO compensation and dark blue bars for Average Non-CEO NEO compensation, while the right vertical axis tracks "Net Income" represented by a black trendline. Overall, Net Income and Average Non-CEO NEO compensation show a steady upward trend from FY2020 to FY2022, while CEO compensation decreases slightly in FY2021 before rising to its highest level in FY2022.

This image features a dual-axis combination bar and line chart titled "Compensation Actually Paid vs. Core PPNR," covering the fiscal years FY2020 through FY2022. The left vertical axis tracks compensation in millions of dollars represented by light blue bars for "CEO CAP ($M)" and dark blue bars for "Average Non-CEO NEO CAP ($M)," while the right vertical axis tracks "Core PPNR" depicted as a dark blue line. Overall, the chart demonstrates an upward trajectory for all three metrics by FY2022, with executive compensation and Core PPNR reaching their highest levels in the final fiscal year shown.

This graphic presents a composite demographic breakdown divided into four quadrant panels covering Age, Gender, Race, and Tenure. The "Age" section uses a donut chart to illustrate the distribution of individuals across age brackets from the 40s to 70s alongside the average age, while the "Gender" panel displays a horizontal bar chart comparing female and male counts. The bottom panels feature a vertical bar chart for "Race" categorizing individuals as White or racially diverse, and a pie chart for "Tenure" showing the breakdown by years of service along with the overall average tenure.

This image is a chevron-style timeline graphic depicting the vesting schedules for long-term incentive equity awards granted in 2021 across a multi-year period extending through 2024. It compares two primary categories of equity awards: Restricted Stock Units and Performance Stock Units. The graphic illustrates that Restricted Stock Units vest incrementally over three consecutive years (2022 through 2024), whereas Performance Stock Units follow a single cliff vesting structure in 2024 after being granted in 2021.

This line chart titled "Total Return Performance" plots cumulative index values across annual periods ending from December 31, 2014, to December 31, 2019. It compares the total returns of Columbia Banking System, Inc. against the NASDAQ Composite and the KBW Regional Banking Index. All three series start at a baseline value of 100 and show an overall upward trend over the five-year span, with Columbia Banking System leading through most of the timeframe before being surpassed by the NASDAQ Composite by the end of 2019.
